title: Dushu, brother of Dudu

paragraphs: Mentioned at the end of Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:2. He gave his wife a divorce document, and the Sages ruled that she should pay the scribe’s fee.

notes.text: The frozen text reads גן, “garden,” and זכר הסופר, “the scribe’s remembrance.” The corresponding Jerusalem Talmud Gittin4:2 passage concerns divorcing a wife and paying the fee. Get and scribe’s fee are contextual proposed readings, not canonical Hebrew repairs.

Hyman (vol. I, p. 327) prints the end of halakhah 2, a get (גט) and the scribe’s fee (שכר הסופר), where the supplied Hebrew has בה״ב, גן and זכר הסופר. Guggenheimer’s Jerusalem Talmud Gittin 4:2 describes Dushu divorcing his wife and the Sages ruling that she pay the fee. The passage goes on to contrast this with the case in which the husband pays.
